title: PetChecker
summary: A mobile app that recommends dog food based on a profile of your dog, designed in Figma for the Google UX Design Certificate. I took it from wireframes to a clickable prototype, tested it with six people in Maze, and revised the design based on what they told me.
alt: Three phone screens from the PetChecker app prototype: an Add your Pets Info form, a completed profile for a dog named Lassie, and the home page showing a matching dog food and a bar chart of steps walked this week.

title: Self-portrait by the river
summary: A flat, painted self-portrait layered over one of my own photographs: sunlight sparkling on a river, an old tree trunk, and autumn leaves floating by.
alt: Digital illustration of a smiling woman with long dark brown hair, black glasses and a grey hoodie, drawn in flat colors and placed over a real photo of a sunlit river with sparkling water, a tree trunk and floating autumn leaves.

title: Friends
summary: Three friends squeezed into one happy frame, drawn in simple flat shapes and bold colors against a bright blue sky.
alt: Digital illustration of three smiling friends leaning together against a blue sky: one with round purple glasses on the left, one in the middle with black glasses, curly brown hair and a green T-shirt with arms folded, and one on the right with shoulder-length brown hair and a black jacket.

title: Through the lens
summary: A relief print of an eye seen through a pair of glasses, carved by hand into a block so that hundreds of flowing lines sweep around the eye like a fingerprint.
alt: Black-and-white relief print of an extreme close-up of an eye behind thick dark glasses. Hundreds of fine curved lines sweep around the eye like a fingerprint, a bushy eyebrow sits above, and two bright white streaks show light reflecting off the lens.

title: Windham Parks & Recreation
summary: A logo for the Windham Parks & Recreation department in Windham, Maine: four circles showing biking, canoeing, fishing and ice skating, wrapped in an oval with the tagline “Find It Here.” It was on the department’s website by 2016 and stayed there until 2025, when it was replaced by a new logo.
alt: The Windham Parks & Recreation logo shown twice, on white and on black: an oval with a lavender border and the words Windham Parks & Recreation in flowing script across the top. Inside are four overlapping circles: a cyclist under a yellow sun beside a daisy, a person paddling a canoe, a person fishing from the canoe among cattails, and an ice skater on snow. Find It Here is written in blue at the bottom.

title: Eric’s Miniatures
summary: A logo for Eric’s Miniatures, a site showing miniatures, terrain and model kits. A jagged orange tear runs through the lettering, and a single slit-pupil eye forms the I in “Eric’s.” It has a light-mode and a dark-mode version, which switch with the site’s theme. Designed in 2020 and still in use on the site.
alt: The Eric’s Miniatures logo shown twice. On white: the words Eric’s Miniatures in chunky lime-green capital letters, split by a jagged orange tear, with a black slit pupil standing in for the I in Eric’s. Below, on dark charcoal: the same logo, where the eye has a white surround so it stands out on the dark background.

title: My own logo
summary: The logo at the top of this website: an A in blue and an S in yellow, set beside my name. It has a second version with light lettering, so it stays readable when the site is in dark mode.
alt: The Amy Sutherland logo shown twice. On a cream background: a large blue A overlapping a yellow S, beside the name Amy Sutherland in black, with Sutherland in bold. Below, on a near-black background: the same logo with the name in off-white.

title: BlackJack
summary: My introduction to JavaScript: a blackjack game I built for a college class in 2016 to learn how the language works. Deal, hit or stand against a dealer who draws to 17, right here in your browser. The playing card art isn’t mine; it came with the class.
alt: Screenshot of the BlackJack game: a green felt table with the title BlackJack at the top and Instructions, Play, Hit and Stand buttons in the corner. The player's hand of 5, 4 and Queen totals 19, the dealer's hand of 3, 5 and King totals 18, and a banner reads You Win! 19 beats the dealer's 18.
